name: Thomas
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: Called Didymus; the apostle who said, “My Lord and my God.”
story: One of the Twelve, called Didymus, who would not believe the others' report of the risen Jesus until he saw Jesus himself eight days later.

entries.title: Called Didymus, “twin”
entries.text: John three times adds that Thomas was “called Didymus” (John 11:16; 20:24; 21:2). Thomas in Syriac and Didymus in Greek both mean “twin” (Thurston, 1912). Scripture never says whose twin he was.

verses.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

verses.text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
¶ And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

quote.text: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;

claim.text: Thomas is named among the twelve chosen (Luke 6:15). No account of his calling is given.
“The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord” (John 20:25).
“There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael” when Peter said “I go a fishing” (John 21:2–3).
With him in the boat by the sea (John 21:2).
The Edessa document quoted by Eusebius says that “Thomas, one of the twelve apostles, under divine impulse sent Thaddeus”, one of the Seventy, to Edessa.

argument.text: The apostles divide the world by lot and “India fell unto Judas Thomas”. He goes unwillingly, sold as a carpenter to a merchant of King Gundaphorus.

A king named Gondophernes or Guduphara ruled in north-west India about AD 20–46, known from coins and the Takht-i-Bahi inscription, and his name matches the Gundaphorus of the Acts. Thurston adds that a romancer may have borrowed real names.
By order of King Misdaeus, four soldiers take him up a mountain and “pierced him with their spears”; later a brother takes his bones “unto Mesopotamia”.
Relics of Thomas were at Edessa in the 4th century; the tradition that he died at Mylapore near Madras is locally strong, but Thurston finds it hard “to discover any adequate support” for it.

items.q: Scripture never says whose twin Thomas was.
John 20:27–29 does not say that Thomas touched the wounds; it records Jesus’ invitation and Thomas’s answer, “My Lord and my God.”
Scripture gives no trade or home for Thomas, and nothing after Acts 1:13.

verses.43011001: Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
verses.43011007: Then after that saith he to his disciples, Let us go into Judæa again.
verses.43011008: His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?
verses.43011009: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
verses.43011010: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no light in him.
verses.43011011: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
verses.43011012: Then said his disciples, Lord, if he sleep, he shall do well.
verses.43011013: Howbeit Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep.
verses.43011014: Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.
verses.43011015: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.
verses.43011016: Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
verses.43014005: Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?
verses.43014006: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
verses.43014007: If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
verses.43020019: ¶ Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.
verses.43020024: ¶ But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
verses.43020025: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.
verses.43020026: ¶ And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
verses.43020027: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
verses.43020028: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
verses.43020029: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
verses.43021001: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself.
verses.43021002: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
verses.43021003: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
verses.44001012: Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.
verses.44001013: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
